identity.title: Engineering Synthetic Molecular Operations Controlled by DNA-Binding Proteins Through Templated Proximity.

content.abstract: We describe a DNA-based molecular framework that enables DNA-binding proteins (DBPs) to perform diverse synthetic operations beyond their natural functions. We introduce templated proximity as a mechanism through which DBP-DNA recognition events are converted into programmable DNA strand displacement reactions. In this architecture, protein binding templates the spatial colocalization of split DNA components, generating functional nucleic acid outputs that can be propagated into downstream processes. Using representative DBPs, including EGR1, YY1, and p53, we couple protein recognition to DNA strand displacement, activation of a fluorogenic RNA aptamer, regulation of CRISPR-Cas12a and Cas13 activity, and DBP-triggered activation of hierarchical CRISPR cascades. These results establish templated proximity as a general transduction principle for integrating DNA-binding proteins into modular nucleic acid reaction networks and demonstrate that DBPs can function as programmable interfaces connecting natural biomolecular recognition with engineered DNA-based information processing, enabling modular communication layers with tailored synthetic functionality.
